newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- MAJOR FACES EU WRATH OVER LINK-UP BY AIRLINES

Prime Minister John Major has been on the receiving end of criticism from the European Commission over the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines . He told the House of Commons that Britain and not Brussels would have the final say in deciding whether the link-up was approved. He said that the Office of Fair Trading would consider representations made by the competition commissioner, Karel van Miert, in preparing advice to trade and industry secretary Ian Lang. Van Miert has warned that he will take Britain to the European Court of Justice unless the airlines were forced to make concessions.
-- BARINGS ACCUSED OVER 1.5 MLN STG FOR ADVISING INVESTMENT FUND

ING Barings, the merchant bank, is being accused of charging an unjustified fee of more than 1.5 million stg for advising an investment fund, even after a majority of investors had accepted alternative proposals. Hessel Lindenbergh, Barings chairman, has refused a demand to repay $1.5 million of the $2.7 million fee and the directors of the Malaysia Equity Fund have asked for an investigation from regulators at the Bank of England and the Securities and Futures Authority.
-- MENZIES SUFFERS TOY SALES FALL

Shares in John Menzies have fallen due to a slump in Christmas toy sales at its Early Learning Centre (ELC) chain. Managing director David Mackay said the fall in sales would lead to a shortfall in expected profits for John Menzies' financial year to the end of April. He said that sales in its high street newsagents and the ELC shops were six million stg below expectations in the eight weeks to December 28.
THE TIMES
-- STRONG POUND ALLOWS CLARKE TOP LEAVE RATES UNCHANGED

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke has said that sterling's strength is the main reason why he has decided to leave interest rates unchanged at six percent for the time being. This comes after the monthly meeting with the Governor of the Bank of England Eddie George. Clarke said that the pound's sharp rise takes away the value of what British exporters are selling. His view gained immediate support from Government statisticians, who say the pound is to blame for falling high street inflation in December.
-- SCOTAM IN 3,000 STG PAYOUT BONANZA

One million policy holders with Scottish Amicable are set to share a bonuses worth up to 3,000 stg after announcing plans to demutualise and float within three to five years. ScotAm announced a two stage reconstructuring which begins with shedding its mutual status. It will pay a special bonus of 75 million stg to members, followed by further benefits at flotation worth 200 million stg.
-- NEWCASTLE TO SHOW LOSSES OF 17 MILLION STG

The publication of Newcastle United football club's prospectus for its spring flotation will show the club has losses of 17 million stg for the year to July 31. The float will value the club at between 160 and 200 million stg. The club said it will raise between 40 and 50 million stg in the float. Joint chief executive, Mark Corbidge, said the money would be used to restructure Newcastle's balance sheet and it may return to the market to raise money to pay for building its new 65 million stg stadium.
THE GUARDIAN
-- REBUKE NUMBER TWO FOR RAILTRACK

Privatised rail company, Railtrack, has received its second reprimand in a month for failing to invest 700 million stg on vital maintenance. Rail industry watchdog John Swift said Railtrack's stewardship was disappointing and unacceptable. He has demanded that the company make public how it will demonstrate its committment and capability to deliver an infrastructure investment programme which meets objectives. Observers say Swift's move is a sign that his patience is wearing thin over the matter.
-- SHELL SIGNALS PLAN TO BECOME BIG PLAYER IN POWER MARKET

Shell, the oil group, has signalled its intention to become a major player in the electricity market despite being at the centre of two environmental rows, over the Brent Spar oil rig and the Ogoni people in Nigeria. The creation of a new part of the group could involve acquisitions of power generation companies such as PowerGen as well as distribution operations which sell to the public.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SIEMENS CHIEF LAMENTS 'UK EUROPHOBIA'

Jurgen Gehrels, chief executive of Siemens in the UK, has made one of the strongest attacks from the business community on the Government's hostility towards joining the single European currency. He said the company would never have committed itself to investing up to 1.1 billion stg in a new micro-chip plant on North Tyneside if he had realised the UK would decide to stay out of the single currency.
-- BZW CAPITALISES ON RIGHTS AUCTIONS

BZW have joined the City's move towards cutting the cost of rights issues through an auction of the sub-underwriting, with a 35 million stg fund raising for car parts distributor Finelist. Schroders and Kleinwort Benson are the only merchant banks to employ auctions of the sub-underwriting to cut the costs for clients. The BZW auction is the sixth to be launched by a City investment bank since last October, and is part of a campaign to persuade the Office of Fair Trading not to refer the fixed commission system to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission for investigation.
-- LORD HARRIS MAKES 23 MILLION STG PRE-TAX PROFIT

Chairman of the Carpetright retail group, Lord Harris of Peckham, made a pre-tax gain of 23 million stg when he sold four million shares in the company, saying the sale was for "estate" reasons so he could avoid the payment of inheritance tax. He says he plans to use the proceedings to buy paintings and other works of art which he could pass on to his four children.
